CLAUDE.md — uci

Source: CLAUDE.md

uci is an R package that calculates the Urban Centrality Index (UCI) as in Pereira et al. (2013) doi:10.1111/gean.12002. The UCI measures how far the spatial organisation of a city or region sits between extreme polycentric (0) and extreme monocentric (1). Published on CRAN; developed at Ipea (GitHub org ipea). Maintainer: Rafael H. M. Pereira. License MIT. Docs: https://ipea.github.io/uci/. Default branch: main.

Core principles

  • Correct numbers first. The package returns one index; a silently wrong value is the worst possible bug. Any change to the computation needs a before/after comparison of uci() output on grid_bho.rds (all four dist_type × bootstrap_border combinations, seeded) and an explanation of every difference.
  • Never surprise the caller. uci() does not modify the user’s sf object, global options, environment variables or the RNG beyond what it restores.
  • CRAN-ready at all times. R CMD check --as-cran: 0 errors, 0 warnings.
  • Plan first. Enter plan mode before non-trivial tasks. Every plan is reviewed by two adversarial agents (Minimalist + Skeptic) that improve it and make it simpler, with as little code intervention as possible. Present the plan only when both reach consensus (max 3 rounds, then escalate the disagreement). Plans live in quality_reports/plans/.
  • Verify after. Every task ends with the gates below, not with “should work”.
  • Learn from corrections. Log [LEARN:category] wrong → right in MEMORY.md.
  • Code style. Always use the convention package::function(). Exception: ggplot2 functions in the vignette and README.

Conventions are in .claude/rules/r-package-conventions.md; gates are in .claude/rules/quality-gates.md.

How uci() works (R/uci.R): 1. Validate inputs; reproject to EPSG:3857; replace NA in var_name with 0. 2. Location coefficient LC = ½ Σ|xᵢ − 1/n| on the normalised distribution. 3. Observed Venables spatial separation V = bᵀ D b, with D the Euclidean (centroids, fields::rdist) or spatial-link (queen contiguity, spdep + cppRouting shortest paths) distance matrix, plus a self-distance sqrt(area/π) on the diagonal (Crafts & Mulatu 2006). D is built in row blocks (venables_blockwise()), never as a full n × n matrix. 4. Max Venables from activities spread along the border cells: one heuristic configuration (bootstrap_border = FALSE, mean(D_border)) or 400 × 50 random border configurations (TRUE, mean(D_border[u, u]) each). parallel sets the spatial-link shortest-path threads (FALSE = 1 thread). 5. UCI = LC × (1 − V / V_max); returns a one-row data.frame (UCI, location_coef, spatial_separation, spatial_separation_max).

Local-only workflow files (gitignored and Rbuildignored): MEMORY.md, quality_reports/, templates/, and everything in .claude/ except rules/.

Commands

devtools::load_all()
devtools::document()                         # regenerate man/ + NAMESPACE
devtools::test()                             # full suite (slow: bootstrap + parallel)
devtools::check(args = "--as-cran")          # long; run in background
lintr::lint("R/<file>.R")                    # no .lintr yet: lintr defaults
pkgdown::build_site()
covr::package_coverage()
  • Run R through the PowerShell tool or from script files: > and | inside Rscript -e '...' are mangled by the shell (see MEMORY.md).
  • bootstrap_border = TRUE evaluates 20,000 border configurations (cheap submatrix means); parallel = TRUE lets cppRouting use all cores for spatial-link distances, so keep it out of CRAN tests and examples.

Quality gates (summary)

Checkpoint Must hold
Commit document() produces no content drift (git diff); devtools::test() passes; lintr clean on changed lines; numeric before/after recorded if the computation changed; NEWS.md entry for user-facing changes
Push / PR check(--as-cran) gives 0 errors / 0 warnings, NOTEs triaged; review loop converged; r-package-reviewer 0 CRITICAL/MAJOR
Release /uci-package-check; win-builder + R-hub; cran-comments.md updated

Details: .claude/rules/quality-gates.md.

Skills and agents

These are local to the maintainer’s Claude setup and are not in git. In a fresh clone, follow the rules in .claude/rules/ directly.

Project skills carry a uci- prefix so user-level skills with the same base name can’t shadow them. In this repo, always use the uci- version (/uci-commit, not a generic /commit). Where user-level rules conflict with .claude/rules/, the project rules win.

  • /uci-package-check: document, test, check --as-cran, triage, reviewer report.
  • /uci-commit: Gate 1, then commit. Push only when asked, after Gate 2.
  • /uci-diagnose: root-cause a failing test or a wrong UCI value.
  • /uci-deep-audit: repo-wide consistency audit (docs ↔︎ code ↔︎ NEWS ↔︎ DESCRIPTION).
  • /uci-checkpoint, /uci-compress-session, /context-status: session state.
  • /uci-learn: turn a session discovery into a reusable skill.
  • Agent r-package-reviewer: read-only CRAN, convention and numerical review of package source.

Working mode

  1. Plan: for non-trivial tasks, enter plan mode, explore, ask only about real decisions, pass the adversarial plan review, and get approval.
  2. Execute (contractor mode): after approval, work autonomously through implement → verify → parallel review → fix, looping until reviews come back dry (see .claude/rules/orchestrator-protocol.md). Come back only for ambiguity or a decision that belongs to the user.
  3. Report: summarise what changed, gate results, open questions; log the session.

No commits, pushes, PRs, version bumps or .github/workflows/ changes without an explicit request. Never hand-edit generated files (NAMESPACE, man/*.Rd, docs/).
